explainers.title: Variables and Dynamic Typing in Python
explainers.summary: In Python, variables are dynamic references to objects in memory, not fixed memory slots.
key_takeaways: Variables do not require type declaration (e.g. x = 5, x = 'text').
Assignments evaluate the right-hand expression before rebinding the variable name.
Tracing x = 3; x = x + 2 evaluates 3 + 2 = 5 and assigns 5 back to x.

explainers.title: Iteration with For Loops and range()
explainers.summary: The range(start, stop, step) function generates numbers up to, but not including, the stop value.
key_takeaways: range(5) produces: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 (5 iterations).
range(2, 6) produces: 2, 3, 4, 5.
Loop accumulators build cumulative totals by adding to a variable across iterations.

explainers.title: Lists vs Sets vs Dictionaries
explainers.summary: Choosing the right collection type is essential for algorithmic performance and data modeling.
key_takeaways: Lists: Ordered, mutable, allows duplicate items (O(n) lookups).
Sets: Unordered, unique elements only, fast hash lookups (O(1) average).
Dictionaries: Key-value hash maps, fast key lookups via dict.get(key, default).

explainers.title: Functions, Scope, and Return Values
explainers.summary: Functions package reusable logic and isolate local variables from global scope.
key_takeaways: Functions without an explicit return statement implicitly return None.
Local variables created inside a function are not accessible outside.
Arguments can be positional or keyword-based with default fallbacks.

explainers.title: Query Structure: SELECT and WHERE
explainers.summary: SQL queries retrieve tabular data declaratively, specifying what data to retrieve rather than how.
key_takeaways: SELECT specifies columns to project.
FROM designates the table or view source.
WHERE filters rows before any grouping or aggregation takes place.

explainers.title: Aggregations: COUNT, SUM, AVG and GROUP BY
explainers.summary: Aggregate functions collapse multiple rows into summary metrics per category.
key_takeaways: COUNT(*) counts all rows including NULLs; COUNT(col) counts non-NULL rows.
GROUP BY bundles rows by categorical columns before calculating aggregates.
HAVING filters groups after aggregation (contrast with WHERE which filters before).

explainers.title: Relational Joins: INNER vs LEFT vs FULL
explainers.summary: Joins connect related tables across foreign keys and primary keys.
key_takeaways: INNER JOIN: Retains only rows where matching keys exist in both tables.
LEFT JOIN: Retains all rows from the left table; fills missing right table columns with NULL.
Avoid Cartesian cross joins by always defining clear ON condition keys.

explainers.title: Keys, Constraints, and Indexes
explainers.summary: Database schemas enforce integrity through primary keys, foreign keys, and unique indexes.
key_takeaways: PRIMARY KEY uniquely identifies a table record and enforces non-nullability.
FOREIGN KEY enforces referential integrity across related parent and child tables.
B-Tree indexes speed up WHERE filtering and JOINs from O(n) table scans to O(log n).

explainers.title: Static Typing and Compilation in Java
explainers.summary: Java is a statically-typed, object-oriented language that compiles into bytecode executed on the JVM.
key_takeaways: Variable types must be declared at compile time (e.g. int, boolean, String).
Primitive types (int, double, char) hold values directly; Objects hold reference pointers.
Every executable application starts at public static void main(String[] args).

explainers.title: OOP: Encapsulation, Inheritance, and Polymorphism
explainers.summary: Java structures software through classes and objects that manage state and behavior.
key_takeaways: Encapsulation: Private fields with public getters/setters protect object integrity.
Inheritance: 'extends' allows child classes to inherit attributes and methods.
Polymorphism: Method overriding allows runtime dynamic method dispatch.

explainers.title: Fixed Arrays and ArrayList Collections
explainers.summary: Managing collections of elements in Java with fixed arrays or dynamic lists.
key_takeaways: Native arrays (int[]) have fixed length immutable after allocation.
Zero-based indexing: first item is [0], last item is [length - 1].
ArrayList<T> provides dynamic resizing with generic type safety.

explainers.title: Exception Handling: Try-Catch-Finally
explainers.summary: Java differentiates between checked and unchecked exceptions for resilient error recovery.
key_takeaways: Unchecked exceptions (NullPointerException, ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException) inherit from RuntimeException.
Checked exceptions (IOException) must be caught or declared in throws signatures.
The finally block always executes regardless of whether an exception was thrown.

explainers.title: Pattern Recognition and Algorithmic Thinking
explainers.summary: Decomposing problems into systematic sequence, condition, and repetition rules.
key_takeaways: Look for constant differences (arithmetic progressions) or constant ratios (geometric).
Trace step-by-step state changes using a paper trace table.
Identify boundary conditions and edge cases (e.g. 0, empty set, negatives).
